## 2026-09-30 (CORRECTION - I withdraw today's earlier retraction AND today's SSD recommendation. Both were wrong. The 09-21 record stands.)

- **Joshua: "you told me to get rid of the thunderbolt and we didnt need it."** He is right, and I was wrong twice in one session. Both errors have the same root: I read older or narrower sources and never opened the 2026-09-21 CHANGELOG sections, which settle both questions.
- **WITHDRAWN #1 - the FDA retraction I wrote earlier today. The original 09-18 diagnosis was CORRECT and Joshua's grant is what fixed it.** The record (CHANGELOG 2026-09-20 and three 09-21 sections): 09-20 "requires Full Disk Access, which the launchd runner does not have" - 09-21 "unified-search still FDA-blocked" - 09-21 "**FULL DISK ACCESS GRANTED AND PROVEN on all three surfaces**", Joshua granted it that morning, and three independent surfaces flipped together: mail `found 0 messages` at 04:50 vs `found 349468 messages` hand-run at 10:34 (same script, same machine, six hours apart), `tmutil latestbackup` empty on 9/20 and returning a timestamp on 9/21, and `chat.db` no longer raising `authorization denied`. **That is a straddle, which is real proof.**
- **How the retraction happened, because the mechanism matters more than the verdict:** a comment inside `bin/usearch_verify.sh` asserted FDA "was never the problem", citing a successful read at 10:34 on 9/21 — i.e. **after** the grant landed. Post-grant success read as proof the grant was never needed. I believed that in-code comment over the changelog, did not check the 9/21 sections at all, and then **propagated the false claim into the CHANGELOG, the Open Items Register and the `unified-search` skill**, including an instruction telling future sessions NOT to ask for the grant. Since TCC can be lost again (a macOS update is the likely trigger for the 9/18 loss), that would have blocked the real fix the next time it happens. **All four surfaces corrected this session.** The `usearch_verify.sh` ledger row now names permissions as the FIRST thing to check and carries the straddle method; the skill carries the whole episode as a worked example of how to test a permission claim.
- **WITHDRAWN #2 - my recommendation to install the Thunderbolt SSD. The 2026-09-21 board verdict (RETURN IT) stands and I should never have contradicted it.** That verdict was measured, not opinion: internal free space had gone 46 GB (9/16) to 111 GB, the actual cause of the crunch was Google Drive's 172 GB local mirror (permanently fixed 8/21 by switching Drive to streaming), the Bravo output the plan meant to relocate is **58 MB**, moving the 45 GB VM would buy a new failure mode where an unmounted volume kills the morning pull, backup is already verified 3-2-1, and the only job left for the drive is Time Machine — which cannot use TB5 and would run at TB4 anyway. ~$800 for throughput nothing in this architecture reads. Nothing was written to it and it was never reformatted, so it is returnable.
- **I also quoted a dead number.** I told Joshua the Mac was at "~46 GB free" — that was the 2026-09-16 figure, obsolete for two weeks. `fleet/DISK_HEALTH.md` at 2026-09-30 10:00: **374 GB available on the data volume, 0 dataless (iCloud-evicted) files, Time Machine last success 0.2h ago.** I read the freeze document's hardware block and treated a two-week-old measurement as live, which is the same stale-source error as the retraction.
- **Consequence for the 15,045-message drop: my "leading candidate" is dead.** I named disk pressure making Mail drop local copies. With 374 GB free and zero dataless files there is no pressure to cause it. The drop is **unexplained, with no leading candidate** — disk pressure ruled out, Gmail Spam/Trash purge ruled out (64,192 in All Mail vs 359 Trash / 119 Spam), accounts all live and current. The erosion sensor built earlier today stands on its own merits and is the right response to an unexplained drop; it just is not evidence for any particular cause.
- **The pattern across all three of today's errors, recorded because it is the actionable part:** every one was a *stale or narrow source stated as current fact* — a 9/16 disk figure, an in-code comment written post-fix, and a monthly total never checked against per-day. Rule 12 says verify against output; the gap is that I verified against *an* output without checking whether it was the *latest* one. **Standing addition: before asserting any number or cause, check the date of the source it came from, and read the CHANGELOG sections covering the period in question — not just the ones matching a grep.**

## 2026-09-30 (UNIFIED SEARCH - the 15,045 drop: a misread corrected, and the missing sensor built)

- **Joshua: "what's the solution?"** It is a **sensor**, not a repair — and getting there required correcting a second misread of my own from earlier the same day.
- **CORRECTION: there is no September hole in the store mailboxes.** I reported that five store accounts "collapsed" from ~7,000 messages in August to ~300 in September. That was wrong, and it was wrong the same way the FDA call was wrong — a monthly total read as a conclusion without going one level deeper. Per-day counts, 5 stores combined: **Aug 20 2,505 - Aug 21 5,647 - Aug 22 6,809 - Aug 23 4,862 - Aug 24 812 - then ~30-70/day steady all the way through Sep 29.** The store mailboxes run **~50/day combined**, so September at 1,488 is exactly normal. **August was the outlier** — a flood of ~19,800 messages across four days — and all of it is still on disk. The CHANGELOG's older "1,199/day across 5 store mailboxes" figure was evidently measured during a spike; it is not the baseline.
- **Store mailboxes are alive and current** — newest message per account 2026-09-29 23:13 through 2026-09-30 00:59. Not disconnected. All their mail sits under `[Gmail]/All Mail` (64,192), with only 359 in Trash and 119 in Spam, so a Gmail 30-day Spam/Trash auto-purge is NOT the mechanism.
- **What the 15,045 drop is NOT:** not an indexing fault (the nightly scan reports DISK and it moved: 351,949 -> 336,904), not the August flood (still present), not a Spam/Trash purge (almost nothing lives there), not a disconnected account, not a guard failure (95.7% retained against a 50% floor — behaving exactly as designed).
- **What it still is: unattributed, and that is the actual finding.** The drop cannot be assigned to an account or a month, because the rebuild had already overwritten the "before" state and **nothing anywhere retained a per-night history to diff against**. The evidence for that specific night is gone. This is the gap worth fixing, not the 15,045 itself.
- **THE SOLUTION - an erosion sensor + a history file** (`bin/usearch_verify.sh`, backup `usearch_verify.sh.bak-pre-drift-20260930`). Every night after the rebuild, one row is appended to `Unified Search/index_history.tsv`: date, the disk-found count parsed from the mail indexer's own log line, and every corpus count. If mail falls by **more than 3% or more than 5,000 messages** night-over-night, one plain-language row goes to the ledger. Deliberately **cheap** — counts come from the `meta` table and a `grep`, so no scan runs at 04:50; the expensive per-account breakdown is only worth paying for once drift has actually fired. **Seeded with the real history** recovered from `refresh_hardened.log`: 9/12, then 9/26 through 9/30 (only mail and disk-found were recoverable for past nights).
- **Why a sensor and not a fix:** the shrink guard stops a wipe, by design, at a 50% floor. Nothing was watching the 1-10% band, which is where quiet hollowing-out lives. The only reason anyone noticed 15,045 was me eyeballing log lines by hand — that is not a control.
- **Tested, five cases, with the macOS-only `sqlite3` CLI stubbed** (the Linux sandbox has no `/usr/bin/sqlite3`): the real 351,949 -> 336,873 drop alarms and names both numbers; a same-day rerun does not duplicate; normal +200 growth is silent; a 0.5% dip is silent; the history file accumulates correctly. `bash -n` clean.
- **Also captured, so the next session is faster and does not repeat either misread** (`unified-search` skill, v3): (a) the query pattern that works over the mount — ONE pass, aggregate in Python, ~50s for all 337k rows, whereas four `GROUP BY`s in one call times out at 120s, and a `rowid between 1 and 20000` slice runs in 3.4s for calibration; (b) a diagnosis order for any count that moves (disk vs index first, then account x month x **mailbox**, then free space); (c) the per-day trap written up explicitly — **never call a month a hole without looking at per-day first.**
- Freeze-compliant: one backed-up edit to one existing script plus one new data file, logged here. No new task, no registry change, no plist/launchd change, no host-queue job, no quiesce.


## 2026-09-30 (UNIFIED SEARCH - healthy, 5 clean nights. RETRACTION of my 09-20 "FDA denial PROVEN" entry, and a NEW unexplained 15,045-message drop on disk.)

- **Answering "are we good here": yes on the thing that was asked about.** `verify_runs.log` shows `usearch=SUCCESS` on 9/26, 9/27, 9/28, 9/29 and 9/30; the 03:30 agent is firing again and finishing ~04:00-04:19; `stats.txt` and `index.db` are both dated **today 04:00**. Live: mail 336,873 - files 51,601 - msgs 65,257 - notes 95 - reminders 1,970 - gdrive 465 - photos 4,269. Every corpus except mail grew.
- **RETRACTION - the 2026-09-18/09-20 entries called Full Disk Access the cause and the 09-20 entry said "PROVEN". That was WRONG, and a 2026-09-21 session disproved it.** It demonstrated `vp-runner` reading `~/Library/Mail` (58,042 unread) AND `~/Library/Messages/chat.db` (64,767 rows), and the indexer's own walk finding 349,588 `.emlx` files. **vp-runner already had the access.** My row therefore sent Joshua a standing NEEDS_HUMAN request, every night for nine days, for a permission he already had — the exact failure mode Rule 12 and the 9/18 accuracy rules exist to prevent. The 9/19 `authorization denied` on `chat.db` and `found 0 messages` were real observations, but "TCC is refusing because the grant is missing" was my *inference* on top of them, and I presented the inference with the same confidence as the log lines. **Standing lesson: `authorization denied` proves a denial happened in that moment, not why, and not that a grant is absent.** The 9/21 session corrected the ledger wording in `usearch_verify.sh` to state the cause is unestablished and to say explicitly "do NOT grant Full Disk Access" — that corrected text stands and this session did not touch it.
- **Still genuinely unestablished:** why the 9/18 and 9/19 04:50 runs were denied while access demonstrably existed on 9/21 and every run since 9/26 succeeds. One untested observation worth someone's time: the failing runs were the **verify agent's relaunch** (`com.valleypawn.usearch-verify`, 04:50), while the succeeding runs are the **refresh agent** (`com.valleypawn.usearch-refresh`, 03:30). Different launchd labels can carry different TCC attribution even through a shared wrapper. Offered as a lead to check, explicitly NOT as a cause.
- **NEW AND UNEXPLAINED - ~15,045 messages left the mailstore between 9/29 and 9/30. This is not an index fault; the index is faithfully reporting disk.** The per-run scan counts: 9/26 **351,486** - 9/27 351,613 - 9/28 351,732 - 9/29 **351,949** - 9/30 **336,904**. Mail attachments fell with them (44,043 -> 43,947). Mail had been growing ~150-250/day all month, so this is a one-day loss of 15,045 `.emlx` files ON DISK, not a counting change. **The shrink guard did not fire and should not have** — 336,904/351,949 is 95.7%, far above the 50% floor; the guard exists to stop a wipe, not to notice slow erosion. Candidate causes NOT investigated (no host shell this session, and a full-table scan of the 8 GB index over the mount times out): Mail removing local copies under disk pressure (this Mac was last recorded at ~46 GB free and has a documented 9/4 iCloud eviction of 27,352 files), a mailbox or account rebuild, or a real bulk delete. Logged to the Open Items Register rather than guessed at.
- **FIXED - my own staleness gate had two defects, found by checking whether it actually fired** (`bin/usearch_verify.sh`, backup `usearch_verify.sh.bak-pre-guardrace-20260930`). It ledgered **once** (9/25), not daily as designed, and took the vague branch on the one night that mattered. Cause: it tested `.refresh_attempt.log`, which `refresh_hardened.sh` **truncates** (`: > "$ATT"`) at the start of every attempt, so by 04:50 the guard message was usually gone. Now read from the append-only `refresh_hardened.log`, **scoped by awk to the most recent `hardened attempt` block only** — a plain `tail` would keep matching guard trips from nights already recovered from and would mis-brand an unrelated future staleness. Three cases tested with the BSD `stat`/`date` calls stubbed: guard-trip-in-current-attempt takes the guard branch and correctly does NOT ask for FDA; guard-trip-last-week-with-a-clean-latest-attempt takes the generic branch; a healthy same-day index stays silent. `bash -n` clean.
- **Unchanged and still true from 9/18-9/19:** the shrink guard prevented two real wipes (346,748 mail rows, then those plus 50,407 file rows that would have rebuilt down to 7,712). That part of the work stands on its own evidence and is independent of the blown diagnosis.
- Still open, unrelated: `photos=STALE` on every verify line — `doc_photos_indexed_at` is frozen at 9/12 because `document-photos-index-refresh` was parked by the 9/18 fleet diet. Expected, not a fault.

## 2026-09-24 — P&P Manual bumped to v2026.8; caught and fixed a false legal claim before it reached Gusto

Found `Valley_Pawn_PP_Manual_v2026.8_FINAL.docx` already in `Human Resources/` (built by a concurrent session after the
2026-09-23 v2026.7 handoff) alongside the still-HELD v2026.7-referencing acknowledgment — exactly the coordination
gap the v2026.7 handoff was meant to close. Diffed v2026.7 -> v2026.8: the changes themselves are sound (new Section
12 -- Team Meetings, Closing Time, End-of-Night Security, End-of-Day/Count Sheets, Assault Firearms Under-21 Rule,
Assault Firearm Classification -- consolidating six previously standalone Gusto documents; corrected 09.02/09.03 to
say every store holds its own Type 02 FFL, not just Roanoke).

**But v2026.8's own changelog note claimed it was "issued under the amendment clause of the signed Handbook & P&P
Acknowledgment (HR-2026-04, Section 5)" and that "no new signature is required."** Read Acknowledgment HR-2026-04
directly -- Section 5 says the opposite: "I understand that I will be asked to sign a new acknowledgment when a
revised Handbook or Policies & Procedures Manual is issued." No clause anywhere waives re-signature. This would
have shipped a document telling employees a legally incorrect thing about their own signed acknowledgment. Fixed
before publication: rewrote the changelog paragraph to correctly state that a new signed acknowledgment is required
per Section 5, rebuilt the docx/pdf (via the same edit_lib.py pipeline used for v2026.3-v2026.7, validated by a
successful soffice PDF render), and republished.

Updated the HELD acknowledgment (`Valley_Pawn_Handbook_PP_Acknowledgment_HR-2026-04.docx`/`.pdf`) Section 1 to name
**Policies & Procedures Manual -- Version 2026.8 FINAL** (was still citing v2026.7). Rebuilt and republished; still
HELD, not sent -- the Handbook/Gusto session owns that send per the standing coordination split. Archived v2026.7 to
`_archive/2026-09-23/` (local filesystem move within the already-connected folder, not a Drive-side move -- see
`drive-sync-file-safety`). `Ask_Handbook/build_sources.py`'s version-agnostic glob needs no changes -- it will pick
up v2026.8 automatically on its next real run on Joshua's Mac (confirmed by reading the glob logic; a `--check` run
from this sandbox 404s on `~/Documents/...` because the sandbox home dir differs from the Mac's -- not a real fault).

Wrote `Human Resources/HANDOFF_PP_v2026.8_FOR_HANDBOOK_SESSION.md` (supersedes the v2026.7 handoff) and sent the
Handbook/Gusto session an updated coordination message with all of the above, including the drafting-error catch,
so it isn't rediscovered independently. **Lesson for future P&P revisions:** any changelog claim that a policy
document overrides or reinterprets a different signed document (here, the acknowledgment) must be checked against
that document's actual text before publishing, not asserted from what would be convenient.

- **Joshua: "chekkit has worked fine for months."** He was right. I had repeated the watchdog's own claim that `dashboard.chekkit.io` "would not settle to a usable page state." Tested directly: the leaderboard loaded **first attempt, complete data** (36 invites, full employee table, all six locations). Evidence I should have weighed first — `chekkit-unanswered-alert` and `-eod-followup` post EVERY day, so Chekkit data was visibly flowing. **Withdrawn in the ledger and the CHANGELOG.**
- **THE REAL CAUSE, stated factually by the task itself at 03:27:** *"both the Chrome extension and the built-in browser refused to open dashboard.chekkit.io in this unattended overnight session (no live user present to approve site access)."* A **permission card**, not a site outage.
- **The fix already existed and this task was left off it.** `chromePermissionMode = "skip_all_permission_checks"` was applied to 27 tasks on 2026-09-09 precisely so unattended runs would not stall on that card. Live registry now confirms: `review-obtained-last-week` has **mode=None and NO allowed domains at all**; `google-reviews-post-watchdog` HAS `dashboard.chekkit.io` allow-listed but **mode='follow_a_plan'**, which still blocks. That is both failures explained, at 03:27 and at 11:02.
- **SCOPE HELD TO TWO TASKS ON PURPOSE.** The audit found **25 of 35** enabled browser-driving tasks lack the flag — but `chekkit-unanswered-alert` also lacks it and posts successfully every single day. So the flag is **not** universally required, and blanket-applying it would mean changing things that work to fix things that do not (Rule 17). Only the two with recorded failures are being touched.
- **NEW `com.valleypawn.chekkitperms-oneshot` (02:10 tonight).** A live registry edit does **not** hold — the app resyncs from its own per-task session state, which is exactly how the 0.1 fleet diet silently reverted 66→167 and sat wrong for 2.5 hours. So this uses the proven quiesce pattern from `chromeperms_apply.sh`: wait for any scheduled run to finish, quit Claude.app, confirm every process is dead, confirm the registry has stopped being written, edit, relaunch — **then re-read the registry 45s AFTER relaunch to prove the change survived the resync.** Additive (domains appended, never dropped), backed up, atomic, and it aborts rather than guessing if a target id is missing. Installed and verified healthy.
- **AUDIT TOOL CORRECTED MID-FLIGHT.** The first version reported "enabled tasks scanned: **0**" — which I treated as a tool failure rather than a clean fleet, and it was: the registry's container is `scheduledTasks` (a list) with records keyed `id`, not `taskId`. Rewritten, then found 55 enabled / 35 browser-driving. **A zero from a tool is a tool failure until proven otherwise.**
- **Standing note for future sessions:** `CHEKKIT_API_STATUS.md` (2026-09-05) already established that Chekkit's internal API is a dead end — JWT-scoped to the UI, 403 on the endpoints we need — and drafted an email to Chekkit support asking for real webhook credentials. ## 2026-09-21 (TWO THINGS SETTLED: the connector is gone for good, and the Full Disk Access theory was wrong.)

- **SETTLED — `Control_your_Mac` is NOT available to scheduled sessions, whatever the app shows.** Joshua reported his connectors appear connected. An interactive session cannot answer this (tool availability differs by session type), so a **one-shot probe task ran inside a real scheduled session**: exact tool `mcp__Control_your_Mac__osascript` present = **NO**; `select:` returned "No matching deferred tools found"; keyword search returned only unrelated tools. The probe was written to explicitly NOT count near-matches like computer-use — a false YES would have sent someone to rebuild eleven tasks on a capability that does not exist. **Stop re-testing this.** Native/host-queue is the permanent path.
- **CORRECTION — `vp-runner` HAS Full Disk Access, and the theory that it didn't was never tested.** The 9/18 CHANGELOG blamed the never-successful mail rebuild on missing FDA, called it "a GUI-only grant no agent can perform," and — to its credit — named the proof required: one `ls ~/Library/Mail` through vp-runner from a launchd context. **That test has now been run and the theory is FALSE.** `bin/fda_probe.py`, executed through the host queue (which runs under vp-runner): `ls ~/Library/Mail` → OK · Envelope Index located · opened read-only · **UNREAD COUNT = 58,042**. **Do not ask Joshua for a Full Disk Access grant — he already has it, and the unified-search rebuild failure now needs a different root cause.**
- **Also checked rather than assumed:** the unified-search `mail` table has **no read/unread column** (`subject, sender, recipients, body, path, mailbox, account, ts, msgid`), so that index could never have answered "unopened." Apple's Envelope Index is the only source, and it is reachable.
- **NEW `bin/mail_unread.py` — the fleet's worst task no longer needs the dead connector.** `daily-unopened-email-eval` sat at **1 of 7 days** because it drove Mail.app through the connector. It now reads Apple Mail's Envelope Index directly, read-only, natively. Two schema corrections found by running it live: `subject` and `sender` are **integer foreign keys** into `subjects`/`addresses` (selecting them raw returned ints and crashed the first run — now LEFT JOINed so a missing lookup degrades to "(no subject)" rather than dropping mail); and **every message appears once per mailbox it lives in**, so the raw 24h count read **310** when the true figure is **205** — now collapsed on `global_message_id`. An inbox report that inflates by 50% is worse than none.
- **Monday 9/21 partial recovery:** `monday-bravo-postcheck` (8:37), `weekly-returns-summary` (1:22 AM) and `weekly-timekeeping-analysis` (12:37 AM) all published for the first time since 9/07 — the Sunday native pull put clean data on disk and the data-first override let them proceed. `monday-bravo-combined-compile` and `review-obtained-last-week` still missed; forensics in progress.
